newsitem.title: USA: Unicom vice chairman named Delta president.
newsitem.headline: Unicom vice chairman named Delta president.

text.p: Unicom Corp said Friday that Leo Mullin resigned as vice chairman of the energy company to become president and chief executive officer of Delta Air Lines Inc, effective immediately.
Unicom spokeswoman Sandra Allen said the company has not made a decision on whether Mullin will be replaced. "The board will deliberate as appropriate," she said.
Allen said that the move was unexpected and that Mullin notified Unicom chairman James O'Connor late yesterday of his plans.

"I leave with deep regret that I will not be able to participate in the enormous success the company will enjoy as deregulation unfolds," Mullin said in a statement. "CommEd (Commonwealth Edison) has enormous competitive advantages which will seve as a strong foundation for its future," he added.

O'Connor praised Mullin's contributions to Unicom. "Leo has rendered extraordinary service to Unicom and Commonwealth Edison for the past 20 months and he has been instrumental in attracting extraordinary talent to work with us," said O'Connor in a news release.
